statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-109478 (GHSA-r3qf-p3jm-8h4p) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue: processing comma-separated HTTP header values allocates an array per value and can exhaust resources; the fix is in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Abstractions (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/2523887d4cca7013afa2737e20cb7f6ba1eed8ff). Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 8.0 runtime, including the linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64 runtime packs, as affected up to 8.0.33 and fixed in 8.0.34 (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-r3qf-p3jm-8h4p, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/515, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.34/8.0.34.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; 8.0.34-r0 is built from the dotnet/dotnet v8.0.134 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v8.0.134). Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships the ASP.NET Core shared framework at its own .NET version, in aspnetcore8-runtime and in the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap: 8.0.23 through 8.0.33 in the earlier builds and 8.0.34 in both 8.0.34-r0 builds. The range ends at 8.0.34-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-109478 (GHSA-r3qf-p3jm-8h4p) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service: processing comma-separated HTTP header values can cause excessive allocations and resource exhaustion. Microsoft fixed it in ASP.NET Core 8.0.34 (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-r3qf-p3jm-8h4p, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/515, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.34/8.0.34.md). The fix is in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Abstractions, which ships in the ASP.NET Core shared framework. DHI dotnet-sdk-8 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK, and the .NET 8.0.34 release notes name .NET SDK 8.0.428 as part of that release. Read the file list of every published dotnet-sdk-8 build for amd64 and arm64: each holds exactly one ASP.NET Core shared framework, under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, plus reference assemblies under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref, and the dotnet-sdk-8-oci-config package from the same source holds only a configuration file and its changelog. The affected builds, with the ASP.NET Core runtime each holds: 8.0.422-0 holds 8.0.28; 8.0.423-0 and 8.0.423-1 hold 8.0.29; 8.0.424-1 holds 8.0.30; 8.0.425-0 and 8.0.425-1 hold 8.0.31; 8.0.426-0 holds 8.0.32; 8.0.427-0 holds 8.0.33. The first build of SDK 8.0.428, 8.0.428-0, and the current 8.0.428-1 hold ASP.NET Core 8.0.34 on both architectures. The 8.0 fix, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/2523887d4cca7013afa2737e20cb7f6ba1eed8ff, makes GetCommaSeparatedValues collect the header values in a ValueListBuilder instead of building a new array for each value. In 8.0.428-0 on both architectures, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Abstractions.dll in the shared framework reports product version 8.0.34+e74b08d77b0c6e9f5d3a99cc2a3807a495f48db3, the v8.0.34 commit of dotnet/aspnetcore, which contains the fix, and contains ValueListBuilder; the 8.0.33 copy in 8.0.427-0 reports the v8.0.33 commit, which does not, and lacks it. The range ends at 8.0.428-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
